title: Meatloaf and Mashed Potatoes
seoTitle: Meatloaf and Mashed Potatoes | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Sunday-dinner energy on a weeknight
description: Sunday-dinner energy on a weeknight. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

ingredients.name: Whole Milk
ingredients.notes: 1/2 cup for the meatloaf, 1 1/2 cups for the mash

steps.title: Mix the meatloaf
steps.instruction: Combine ground beef, breadcrumbs, eggs, diced onion, 1/2 cup milk, 2 tsp salt, and 1 tsp pepper — mix by hand just until combined. Shape into two loaves on sheet pans — two loaves cook faster and slice cleaner for a crew.

steps.title: Bake the loaves
steps.instruction: Whisk ketchup, brown sugar, and vinegar; brush half over the loaves. Bake at 375°F 40 minutes, brush on the remaining glaze, and bake 10–20 minutes more until internal temp hits 160°F and the glaze caramelizes. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.

steps.title: Boil and mash potatoes
steps.instruction: Boil peeled russets until fork-tender. Drain; mash with butter and the remaining warm milk until smooth. Season aggressively with the remaining salt and pepper — bland mash kills comfort food morale.

steps.title: Plate family-style
steps.instruction: Slice meatloaf on a tray; serve mashed potatoes in a warm cambro. Meatloaf & Mashed is pure hall comfort — extra ketchup on the table, no questions asked.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Meatloaf and Mashed Potatoes with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Meatloaf and Mashed Potatoes on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sunday-dinner energy on a weeknight. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use certified gluten-free panko/breadcrumbs, or crushed gluten-free crackers.

adaptable.label: Dairy-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a plant-based butter/margarine. Use oat, almond, or soy milk (check tree-nut/soy status of the substitute).
